# Northvale froze your money. It's safe. And we're as angry as you are.

*By Inês — 10 November 2026*

**If you only read one thing:** your money is safe, and it is not Northvale's money. Northvale, the payments company that holds your balance, blocked every withdrawal from Pinha on Friday 6 November at 09:00 — without warning, and in breach of the 30-day notice they had given us two days earlier. We cannot move your money until they release it. If you have a hard deadline coming — rent, medical, a deposit, a job ending — write to **urgent@pinha.example** with the subject **URGENTE** and we will push for an individual release. We will post an update here every Monday and Thursday until this is over.

---

## First, the email that made me close my phone

This morning, on the metro, I read a message from a customer in Porto. She had written it all in capital letters, which I am not going to reproduce, because it did not need to be in capitals to make the point.

She has been saving for three years for a deposit on a car. The dealership is holding the car for her until Friday, 13 November. Until Friday, she needs to pay. On Friday morning, a machine told her that she cannot take out her own money.

I read it twice on the metro and then had to put my phone away for a minute.

My name is Inês. I design the screens in Pinha. I also wrote the line on our main screen that says *your money is always yours, take it out anytime*. I wrote it because I believed it, and I still believe it — but I have been looking at it for the last four days and feeling physically ill, because for those four days it has not been true.

That is Northvale's doing. It is also, partly, ours. I will get to that, and I am not going to dress it up.

## What actually happened

Here is the timeline, because I would rather you had the facts than a paragraph of corporate sympathy.

- **Tuesday 4 November.** Northvale emailed us a "commercial termination" of our agreement, with 30 days' notice. No real reason was given beyond a phrase about their "risk appetite review". Thirty days. We had time to plan, to migrate, to prepare.
- **Friday 6 November, 09:00.** They blocked all outgoing transfers. No warning, no phone call first, nothing. The same Friday they emailed us to say they were giving us time we did not need, because they had already decided to pull the switch. Deposits stopped too. Round-ups stopped with them.
- **Friday 6 November, afternoon.** I started reading support emails. There were a lot of them.
- **Saturday 7 November.** We filed complaints with Banco de Portugal and with the Bank of Lithuania, Northvale's home regulator.
- **Monday 10 November (today).** This post.

Northvale's account manager stopped answering our calls on Friday. His phone goes to a voicemail in Lithuanian. A company that has frozen 14,200 people's savings cannot get back to its own partner to explain itself.

I am not going to tell you to calm down. I would be furious. If you are angry at Northvale, you are right to be. If you are angry at us as well, that is fair, and I'll take it.

But I want to say one thing plainly, because I think it matters: **this is not "risk management".** A real risk decision looks like cancelling a product, winding down accounts, telling customers early, moving the money somewhere it can be reached. What happened on Friday was a switch being thrown in the dark, with a notice attached afterwards to make it look procedural. That is not caution. That is cowardice, and it cost people their rent and their car deposits.

## Where your money is right now

This is the part I most need you to read carefully, because the phrase "my money is gone" is not true and I don't want you carrying that around for weeks.

Northvale holds your balance in a **safeguarded account**, legally separated from Northvale's own money. Your money is not in their business account. It is not part of their balance sheet. They cannot spend it, lend it, invest it or use it to pay their own staff. It is yours, ring-fenced, and they cannot touch it.

So the money is not lost. It is also not moving.

Here is the honest, frustrating truth: **we cannot release it either.** A safeguarded account cannot be moved by us — it can only be released by the institution that holds it, or as part of a regulated migration to another institution. Until Northvale either releases the funds or hands over the balances in a proper transfer, the money sits exactly where it is. We are not able to override that, and anyone who tells you a support agent can "unlock" your balance from a phone screen is making it up.

Your round-ups have not been running since Friday morning, so the balance you are looking at has not moved either. Nothing has been lost in the meantime. When deposits resume, the round-ups will be made whole — I will not let a single euro of that quietly disappear.

## What we are doing about it

**We have signed a new partner.** Ostra Bank, in Lisbon. The migration is agreed on our side. To complete it, two things have to happen: Northvale has to send us the file of balances, and Banco de Portugal has to approve the transfer of the safeguarded funds.

**On timing, I am not going to give you a date.** The honest position is an estimate of **10 to 15 working days once the balances file reaches us and the approval is in place**. Count from there and you are looking at December. That is an estimate, not a promise, and I know a range is a worse thing to read than a single confident sentence. But if I write a date and December 19 arrives and nothing has moved, you will have lost another week of trust, and you will have every right to be angrier with us than you are today. So: an estimate, and updates every Monday and Thursday — Monday 16 and Thursday 19 November, then every Monday and Thursday after that — even on the days when there is nothing new. Especially on those days.

**We are asking Northvale, through our lawyers and our regulator, to release individual balances** for people with genuine emergencies: rent due, medical bills, a job ending. This is the only lever that can move money before the migration, and it is a slow one. It may not work for everyone. If we cannot get a release for you, I will tell you that directly rather than leaving you waiting.

**Your monthly fee is cancelled for November and December**, for everyone, whether or not you use anything.

**We have filed complaints** with Banco de Portugal and the Bank of Lithuania. If you are in Spain, Banco de España is the right place for your complaint as well. Complaints are not a magic fix, but they are real pressure on a company that currently has nobody answering its phone.

## What you can do today

1. **If you have a deadline — rent, medical, a deposit like the one in Porto, a job ending — email urgent@pinha.example with the subject URGENTE.** Tell us what the money is for and give us the date. Those go to the top of the list for individual release requests.
2. **For everything else, please use the normal support channel and not the urgent address.** Since Friday we have received **1,900 emails**, answered by a team of three. Our reply time is now around **two days**. I know that is a bad number. I know it is worse when the money is your own. I would rather be honest that we are stretched than pretend otherwise.
3. **Please don't try to make new deposits or move money around in the app** while everything is frozen. Transfers in flight during the freeze are the most likely to get delayed or lost, and I would rather you not add anything to the pile.
4. **Keep every screenshot, every bank statement, every message from Northvale** if you have it. Our lawyers will ask for them.

## The part that is our fault

I am a designer. I care a great deal about how a thing feels in the hand, and less than I should about how a thing fails. So let me say the uncomfortable bit without softening it.

**We had one payment partner and no fallback.** One. Not a primary and a backup — one. We chose that for speed and cost, we got away with it for years, and on Friday morning the bill came due for 14,200 people's savings. A single vendor's internal decision could freeze every account, and there was no second rail underneath us to catch it. That is a structural failure and it belongs to the people who built Pinha, which includes me.

We trusted Northvale's licence, their audits, their compliance team, their word — and some of that trust was reasonable. What was not reasonable was trusting them with the one switch that can hold everyone's money still, with nothing behind it and no plan for the day it flipped. We wrote *your money is always yours, take it out anytime* and then built the app in a way where a stranger could take that sentence away on a Friday morning by not picking up the phone. The sentence and the architecture did not match. I wrote the sentence. I also understand, better than I did a week ago, how thin the architecture was underneath it.

I am not going to sit here and ask for your understanding. I would rather earn it back with a finished migration and a system that cannot be held hostage by one company's mood.

## One last thing

I read all 1,900 of those emails as they came in. Some of them are reasonable. Some are furious. Some are just someone asking, very quietly, whether the money is going to be there in December.

I can't answer that yet with a date. What I can tell you is that the money is safe, that we know exactly where it is and who has to release it, that we have a new partner ready to take it, that two regulators are now asking Northvale the same questions we are, and that on Monday and Thursday you will hear from me again.

If you are still angry on Monday: write to me. I'll read it.

— **Inês**, product design, Pinha

reasons: Weekdays are wrong: it calls 10 November 'Monday' (the request says Tuesday), and 4 November 'Tuesday' (it was a Wednesday). It also invents a Friday email saying Northvale was 'giving us time we did not need'.
